findings.description: AWS access key ID and secret access key are hard-coded in plaintext in the instance user_data script, which is stored in the EC2 metadata service and Terraform state, exposing long-lived credentials to anyone with instance or state access.

The EBS volume does not enable the encrypted attribute (it is explicitly commented out), leaving data at rest unencrypted and recoverable if the underlying storage is compromised or snapshots are exposed.
The EBS snapshot inherits encryption from the unencrypted source volume, so the snapshot data is also stored unencrypted and can be shared or copied without protection.

The security group allows inbound TCP port 22 (SSH) from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing the management interface of the instance to the entire internet, and the instance sits in a subnet with map_public_ip_on_launch enabled, making it directly reachable.

map_public_ip_on_launch is set to true, automatically assigning public IP addresses to instances launched in this subnet, increasing internet exposure when combined with the permissive security group.
map_public_ip_on_launch is set to true, automatically assigning public IP addresses to instances launched in this subnet, increasing exposure to the internet.
The S3 bucket used for VPC flow logs has no server-side encryption configuration, allowing potentially sensitive network traffic metadata to be stored unencrypted.
The S3 bucket has no public access block or bucket policy restricting access, and force_destroy is enabled; absence of explicit access controls risks unintended public exposure of flow log data.
